runs.market_commentary:
Asian markets closed sharply lower overnight as tech and semiconductor names bore the brunt of a broad selloff ahead of Nvidia's pivotal Q3 earnings report. Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 1.34% to 58,860 as chipmakers weighed on the index, while South Korea's Kospi dropped 3.6%—among the worst performers globally—on fears that the Commerce Department's new interim rule restricting remote access to advanced AI chips could crimp revenue at Samsung and SK Hynix. China's October industrial production and retail sales both missed consensus estimates, amplifying macro anxieties and dragging the Hang Seng Technology Index more than 2% lower. The yuan edged weaker as market participants priced in a higher probability of additional PBOC easing.

European equities opened under pressure in sympathy with Asian losses and failed to recover meaningfully through the morning session. Germany's DAX shed 1.05% to 26,351, with ASML and SAP leading declines on AI chip export restriction headlines. The FTSE 100 fell 1.10% to 10,773, though AstraZeneca provided a notable bright spot after the FDA approved two new therapies—one for muscle-invasive bladder cancer and one for generalized myasthenia gravis—adding meaningful pipeline de-risking to the company's oncology franchise. Oil also weighed on UK energy names as Brent crude fell roughly 3.5% on reports of recovering Strait of Hormuz oil flows reinforcing expectations of a supply surplus.

U.S. index futures are mixed heading into Tuesday's session, with Nasdaq 100 futures up 0.36% at 27,383 and Dow futures down 0.36% at 51,485 after Monday's brutal tech-led selloff that saw the Nasdaq Composite fall 2.49%. The two headline events of the day are Nvidia's fiscal Q3 earnings after the close—the first report since CEO Jensen Huang's departure, with interim CEO Colette Kress expected to give a detailed AI pipeline update—and the Anthropic IPO, which is expected to price above its last private valuation. Home Depot reported a solid Q3 beat before the open and named CFO Richard McPhail as incoming CEO, while Disney is set to report today with expectations for a 52% YoY EPS gain driven by streaming profitability. U.S. October retail sales data is due at 8:30 AM ET and could add volatility if it surprises versus the consensus flat reading.

ideas.catalyst: Nvidia reports Q3 fiscal 2026 earnings after the close, its first report under interim CEO Colette Kress after Jensen Huang's departure; consensus expects 91% YoY revenue growth to $108.93B and EPS of $2.47.
ideas.thesis: Despite a 35% selloff from recent highs and leadership uncertainty, Nvidia's data center GPU monopoly remains structurally intact as hyperscalers continue to accelerate capex on AI infrastructure. If Kress delivers strong H1 2027 guidance and the data center segment beats the $95B consensus, the stock is likely to see a sharp snap-back toward the $160-170 range.
ideas.key_risk: AI chip export restrictions from the Commerce Department's new interim rule could materially crimp addressable market, and a guidance miss on data center revenue would likely trigger a further 10-15% decline.

ideas.catalyst: Disney reports fiscal Q4 2026 earnings today; Wall Street consensus expects EPS of $1.69 versus $1.11 in the prior year period—a 52% YoY gain—alongside revenue of $25.19 billion.
ideas.thesis: Disney's direct-to-consumer streaming segment has reached sustained profitability and is now a margin accretive business, fundamentally reshaping the company's earnings power versus the legacy linear TV model. A beat on streaming ARPU and paid subscriber net adds, combined with continued parks resilience, could lift shares 4-6% and begin a re-rating toward peers like Netflix.
ideas.key_risk: Any sequential slowdown in parks EBITDA margins or a surprise decline in Disney+ subscribers would overshadow the broader beat and trigger selling into the report.

ideas.catalyst: The FDA approved two AstraZeneca therapies simultaneously: one for muscle-invasive bladder cancer and one for generalized myasthenia gravis, expanding its oncology and rare disease portfolio.
ideas.thesis: Dual FDA approvals in a single day are extremely rare and underscore the depth of AstraZeneca's pipeline. Both indications represent multi-billion dollar addressable markets with limited competition, and the bladder cancer indication in particular gives AZN a first-mover advantage in a space where pembrolizumab has not yet fully penetrated the muscle-invasive segment.
ideas.key_risk: Pricing negotiations under the Inflation Reduction Act and competitive launch by Merck in the same bladder cancer indication could compress net revenue realization below peak sales estimates.

ideas.catalyst: Home Depot reported a fiscal Q3 beat before the open and named CFO Richard McPhail as incoming CEO, replacing Ted Decker; shares are down 1.65% premarket on the news despite the earnings beat.
ideas.thesis: The initial negative reaction to Home Depot's CEO change appears to be an overreaction—McPhail is a known, trusted internal candidate with deep financial expertise, and his appointment provides continuity rather than disruption. The underlying Q3 beat signals that housing renovation demand is holding up better than feared, creating a favorable setup for a reversal of the premarket selloff.
ideas.key_risk: If McPhail's first appearance on the Q3 call reveals a more cautious outlook for housing/renovation spending in 2027, the stock could fail to recover and slide toward the $400 level.

ideas.theme: Goldman Sachs Top Pick / M&A Advisory Recovery
ideas.catalyst: Goldman Sachs named Houlihan Lokey its top 2026 stock pick with 36% upside potential, citing M&A deal volume recovery and the company's leading position in financial restructuring advisory.
ideas.thesis: Houlihan Lokey's mid-market M&A focus and financial restructuring advisory revenues are set to benefit from two simultaneous tailwinds: a recovering deal environment (evidenced by multiple M&A announcements today) and elevated corporate distress in real estate and media. HLI trades at a discount to larger bulge bracket peers despite superior mid-market deal capture rates.
ideas.key_risk: A broad equity market selloff driven by NVDA earnings disappointment or macro data could freeze M&A pipelines and delay fee recognition into 2027.

ideas.catalyst: Eli Lilly announced the acquisition of Calytrix Bio for up to $1.5 billion, targeting AI-powered drug discovery capabilities to accelerate its next-generation pipeline beyond the GLP-1/2 obesity franchise.
ideas.thesis: Lilly's willingness to pay $1.5B for an AI drug discovery platform signals high confidence in its core cash generation from the obesity franchise and strategic intent to diversify. The acquisition price is modest relative to Lilly's market cap, limiting dilution while potentially adding significant optionality if Calytrix's pipeline candidates hit clinical milestones.
ideas.key_risk: Integration of AI drug discovery platforms has a poor track record industry-wide; any early negative trial read-through from Calytrix assets could dampen enthusiasm for the acquisition premium.

ideas.catalyst: Summit Therapeutics listed in pre-market focus headlines alongside Nvidia as a key mover; ivonescimab (AK112) continues Phase 3 development against Keytruda in first-line NSCLC.
ideas.thesis: SMMT's ivonescimab combines PD-1 and VEGF inhibition in a bispecific antibody format and demonstrated superior PFS vs. Keytruda in the HARMONi-2 trial in Chinese patients. If upcoming Western patient cohort data mirror the Chinese results, the drug could represent a multi-billion dollar threat to Merck's keystone franchise and trigger a substantial re-rating of SMMT.
ideas.key_risk: NSCLC bispecific antibodies have shown geographic heterogeneity in efficacy—the Western patient data could fail to replicate the Chinese trial results, causing a 40-60% stock decline.

ideas.catalyst: Flex announced the spinoff of Axiom (data center power & cooling) targeting Q1 2027; shares fell 2.7% on the announcement as uncertainty over stub valuation creates overhead.
ideas.thesis: Spinoff announcements typically create a 3-6 month overhang as index funds and diversified holders sell ahead of the distribution, while pure-play Axiom buyers accumulate post-spinoff. With the transaction set for Q1 2027, there is 4+ months of persistent selling pressure on FLEX, and the remaining RemainCo may not attract a premium multiple without the high-growth Axiom business.
ideas.key_risk: If data center infrastructure sentiment improves materially on strong NVDA guidance, Axiom's valuation could attract strategic buyer interest, causing FLEX to recover sharply and creating a painful short squeeze.

ideas.catalyst: Red Cat Holdings is down 30% in premarket trading, breaking through multiple support levels and printing the largest single-day decline among major small-cap premarket movers.
ideas.thesis: A 30% premarket gap-down in a small-cap stock typically sees follow-through selling at the open as retail holders capitulate, margin calls force liquidation, and momentum algorithms pile on. The sheer magnitude of the move suggests a fundamental catalyst—likely a contract loss or earnings warning—that is not yet fully priced in.
ideas.key_risk: The catalyst driving the decline may already be fully discounted; any short-covering or speculative buying could produce a sharp intraday reversal, as small-cap momentum stocks are prone to violent counter-trend moves.

ideas.catalyst: Alibaba listed in pre-market focus headlines; China's October industrial production and retail sales missed expectations, creating a potential oversold entry point as bad news is priced in.
ideas.thesis: Alibaba trades at a persistent steep discount to U.S. tech peers despite comparable or superior free cash flow generation and a strengthening cloud segment. With the PBOC likely to respond to disappointing October macro data with additional stimulus measures, any forward-looking policy catalyst could compress the discount and drive a 15-20% rebound in BABA ADRs.
ideas.key_risk: Escalating U.S.-China tech tensions from the new AI chip export restriction regime could worsen ADR investor sentiment and trigger further institutional outflows from Chinese technology holdings.

deals.headline: Eli Lilly Acquires Calytrix Bio for Up to $1.5B to Bolster AI Drug Discovery Pipeline
deals.description: Eli Lilly announced the acquisition of Calytrix Bio, a private AI-powered drug discovery platform, for up to $1.5 billion in a deal that closed November 16. The acquisition adds computational drug design capabilities to Lilly's pipeline beyond the GLP-1/2 obesity franchise, targeting novel mechanisms in metabolic disease and oncology.
deals.impact: Modest near-term EPS dilution; long-term pipeline optionality if AI platform yields clinical candidates by 2028-2029

deals.headline: Canadian Natural Resources Acquires Advantage Energy for ~$1.8B
deals.description: Canadian Natural Resources announced an all-share acquisition of Advantage Energy for approximately $1.8 billion, bolstering its Montney natural gas position in northeast British Columbia. TD Cowen noted the offer represents fair value with limited near-term premium for Advantage holders.
deals.impact: Accretive to CNQ's Montney gas production; Advantage holders receive full takeout value at current market price

deals.headline: AstraZeneca Receives Dual FDA Approvals for Bladder Cancer and Myasthenia Gravis Therapies
deals.description: The FDA approved two AstraZeneca therapies on the same day: one targeting muscle-invasive bladder cancer and one for generalized myasthenia gravis, adding to AZN's growing rare disease portfolio. Both approvals represent immediate commercial revenue opportunities estimated in the billions of dollars combined.
deals.impact: Positive: de-risks pipeline and adds two commercial revenue streams; analysts expect upgrades to AZN price targets in coming days

deals.headline: Flex Announces Axiom Spinoff (Data Center Power & Cooling), Targets Q1 2027 Completion
deals.description: Flex Ltd. announced that its Axiom business unit—focused on data center power delivery and thermal management—is on track to spin off as an independent public company in Q1 2027. Flex shares fell 2.7% on the announcement as investors weighed stub valuation and the loss of one of the company's highest-growth segments.
deals.impact: Near-term negative for FLEX as spinoff overhang builds; Axiom pure-play could command premium multiple at IPO given data center infrastructure demand
deals.sentiment: Neutral (short-term bearish for FLEX, long-term positive for Axiom holders)

deals.headline: Anthropic PBC Goes Public via Highly Anticipated IPO, Valued Above Prior $61B Private Round
deals.description: Anthropic PBC, the AI safety company and creator of the Claude AI assistant family, is completing its initial public offering and is expected to price above its last private round valuation of approximately $61 billion. The IPO is being watched as a bellwether for AI sector sentiment and a test of institutional appetite for large-cap AI companies at premium valuations.
deals.impact: Major positive sentiment catalyst for the broader AI sector; could attract institutional capital reallocation from other AI names toward the new public company

key_events.impact: Highest possible market impact; consensus expects $108.93B revenue (+91% YoY) and $2.47 EPS

key_events.impact: Medium-High: EPS expected +52% YoY; streaming subscriber trajectory key variable

key_events.impact: Medium: consensus expects flat reading; a miss could dampen consumer discretionary names

key_events.impact: Medium-High: restricts foreign access to US AI computing infrastructure; negative for hyperscalers with international AI cloud operations

key_events.impact: Medium: signals systemic monitoring of AI infrastructure leverage; potential for future macroprudential policy response
